title: First Class
tagline: Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns for book launches at First Class Publishing.
lead: Concepts and design for paid and organic campaigns at First Class Publishing, created in-house: new books, events and seasonal occasions, running on Meta with a monthly ad spend of €5,000–10,000.

title: Space Karlín
tagline: Wayfinding system for a café and coworking space in Prague’s Karlín district.
lead: A café that was hiding its own coworking floor. A wayfinding system in metal and glass now makes every service visible and every room easy to find, without disturbing a deliberately minimal interior.
deliverables: Wayfinding strategy, menu wall, printed menus (CZ / EN) and Christmas menu, directional and room signage, zone pictograms and rules, QR table stickers, locker signage, kitchen signage, window graphics, production supervision
description: Space Cafe combines a café with coworking at two Prague locations. Most guests are office workers buying coffee to go; a smaller group stays to work, using day coworking, meeting rooms and a podcast studio on the second floor.
task: The interior — raw concrete, glass and many identical doors — gave no cues about where to go, and many guests never discovered that coworking existed. The system had to make these services visible from the café, guide visitors through the upper floor and explain how each zone works, using as little text as possible.
solution: The wayfinding was planned as a sequence that follows the visitor: awareness at the bar, direction on the stairs and in the corridors, rules at each door. Materials were chosen to belong to the architecture — metal lettering mounted directly on concrete, vinyl on glass — and the café’s own typeface ties everything together. The project covered the full process, from navigation logic and on-site measurements to production files and coordination with the workshop.

title: Tomas Arsov
tagline: A series of YouTube thumbnails for Tomas Arsov’s hair care products — bold, consistent and instantly recognizable.

title: la FORMULA
tagline: Christmas label design for la FORMULA’s Stromeček and Svařák candles.
lead: For its Christmas collection, a minimalist Brno candle brand wanted something warmer: labels with the charm of a vintage holiday postcard. Four labels extend the brand’s existing system into a seasonal edition without breaking it.
deliverables: Four labels (two scents, two sizes), illustration art direction
description: la FORMULA hand-pours soy-wax candles and home fragrances in a small studio in Brno. Its everyday look is clean and minimal. The Christmas edition centres on two classic Czech holiday scents: Stromeček (Christmas tree) and Svařák (mulled wine), designed to be given as gifts and kept on display.
concept: A seasonal edition that still belongs to the family. The frame of la FORMULA’s standard label stays, preserving recognition on the shelf. A tartan border and vintage-style illustrations add the festive layer: a decorated tree for Stromeček, a snowy Christmas market for Svařák. The illustrations were generated with AI and art-directed through many iterations until they matched the look and warmth of genuine vintage prints.

title: WannaSurf
tagline: Mobile-first sales presentation for a surf camp in Morocco.
lead: A surf camp that chose not to build a website needed another way to sell. The answer is an interactive vertical presentation that works like a mini-site on the phone: it conveys the atmosphere, answers every practical question and leads straight to booking.
deliverables: Interactive PDF presentation with navigation and booking links
description: WannaSurf runs week-long surf camps in Morocco for beginners and experienced surfers, combining lessons with shared meals, excursions and evenings by the fire. The founders’ personal approach and the sense of a group becoming a family are at the core of the offer. The presentation was produced for a Russian-speaking audience.
task: Replace a website with a single document sent to every prospective guest. It had to sell an emotional experience and, at the same time, explain the programme, accommodation, food and pricing clearly enough to remove any doubt before booking.
solution: The format was designed around how people actually opened it: on their phones. A portrait layout with tappable buttons and links turns the PDF into a lightweight mobile site. The structure follows a guest’s decision path — price and what’s included first, then surfing, accommodation, community, programme, food, activities and the team — with a clear route to booking from every page.

title: The Secret Garden
tagline: Self-initiated identity for an imaginary winery and hotel in a historic country house.
lead: A hotel conceived as a hideaway, a place not everyone finds. The identity is built around that idea of a private threshold, and it starts with a key.
deliverables: Logo, colour and type system, letterhead, envelopes, key tags, postcards, welcome letter
description: A self-initiated project exploring a complete identity for a boutique winery and hotel set in an old house, where winemaking tradition meets art, comfort and attention to detail. Without a client brief, the project set its own standard: every touchpoint, from the logo to the wine list, should belong to the same world.
concept: The key is the brand’s central idea: a secret garden is a place you have to be let into. Its bow is drawn as a leaf from the garden, and its bit traces the silhouette of the house. Archival landscapes and botanical paintings place the brand in a building with a long history, Instrument Serif gives it a classic, literary voice, and a deep wine red marks the moments that matter.

title: Mynds Festival
tagline: A bold, multicolour identity for a popular-science festival where different minds meet.
lead: Mynds is a popular-science festival about living a calmer, more fulfilling life. Its identity was built from scratch around a name that reads three ways and a colour system that gives each of the festival’s seven life areas its own voice.
description: Mynds brings 150+ Czech and international experts and 10,000+ visitors together around seven areas of life: body, mind, work, learning, family, love and soul. All talks are commercially independent. The audience is unusually broad, from secondary-school students and their teachers to parents, working adults and older visitors.
task: Create a complete identity from zero, including a distinct look for each of the seven areas. It had to feel bold, modern, energetic and authentic, speak equally to teenagers and their grandparents, and keep seven very different topics together as one festival. The working title, BOLD, was dropped mid-process when a festival of the same name turned up in Brno.
solution: A flexible system: a logo in two versions (with and without descriptor), a mint core palette with black, white and grey, seven area colours and pictograms, and two typefaces. It extends to posters, the programme, tickets, wristbands, social media and merchandise, as well as festival visualisations for the website and investor presentations.

title: Rubin Production
tagline: Brand identity and digital presence for a Prague video and photo production studio.
lead: A production studio needed a brand as considered as the footage it delivers. The answer is a geometric mark designed for motion from day one, and a visual language borrowed directly from the camera.
deliverables: Logo and logo animation, brand guidelines, business cards, gift certificates, YouTube and Instagram design, website design, Rubin Catering sub-brand
description: Rubin Production is a Prague studio producing video, photography and live streams for small and medium-sized businesses, bloggers and public figures. The name comes from the founder’s surname; in Czech and Russian, rubín is the deep red gemstone. Rubin has been a client since 2020, and the brand has grown with the studio.
task: Create an identity from scratch, starting from a client moodboard. The mark had to signal the studio’s field without category clichés such as film reels or clapperboards, and be ready for animation. The brand needed to make an immediate impression: professional and reliable to business clients, creative and contemporary to everyone else.
solution: The identity rests on two decisions. The first is a compact geometric mark built from simple planes, so it holds at small sizes and animates naturally on screen. The second is a framing device taken from the studio’s own equipment, the camera viewfinder, which turns every layout, from business card to Instagram post, into a frame from a Rubin shoot. A red-to-burgundy gradient on black sets a cinematic, premium tone.

gallery.label: Concept
gallery.title: The mark
gallery.text: The mark combines three symbols: the letter R, a ruby, the gem behind the studio’s name, and a play button for its work in photo, video and animation. A clean geometric form keeps it precise, versatile and ready for motion.

gallery.label: @rubinproduction.eu
gallery.title: Instagram
gallery.text: Story highlight covers and post templates that introduce the studio, its services, studio rental and prices at a glance, in the same dark palette with red accents as the rest of the brand.

gallery.label: @rubincatering
gallery.title: Rubin Catering
gallery.text: A sub-brand for the studio’s catering: the R becomes a C, while the geometry, colours and Instagram system stay the same, so both brands read as one family.

title: Iris ateliér
tagline: Identity and packaging for a Prague atelier, rooted in the French couture tradition.
lead: A small Prague atelier whose clients often arrive with Dior in mind. The identity answers that ambition with a classic French vocabulary: toile de Jouy, botanical engraving and a single blue-lilac drawn from the iris itself.
role: In-house designer, the atelier’s first employee
deliverables: Logo, colour and type system, gift box, wrapping paper, tags, stickers, business cards, letterhead, garment-care letter, door signage, website design
description: Iris ateliér offers tailoring, alterations and embroidery on clothing. Many clients come in with references from the great couture houses and ask for pieces in the same spirit, which set the level the brand had to meet.
task: Replace an outdated logo with an identity that is minimal and elegant, appeals to a female clientele and conveys the care behind every garment, from the first fitting to the moment a finished piece is handed over.
solution: Rather than inventing new ornament, the identity borrows from the visual history of fashion. An adapted toile de Jouy, the classic French printed textile, becomes the brand’s signature surface, and an archival iris engraving speaks the same language. Both are restricted to one colour, so the system is rich in detail yet calm overall. Packaging carries most of the brand experience: unwrapping is the moment the atelier’s care becomes tangible.

gallery.title: Concept
gallery.text: A typographic logo — minimalist and sophisticated. The Iris Atelier logo reflects the brand’s core values: femininity, elegance and aesthetics. It looks great on business cards, packaging and tags, and despite its simplicity it catches customers’ attention.

title: Alla Vakker
tagline: Personal brand and website for a Prague-based portrait and brand photographer.
lead: A photographer whose images are bold, colourful and often daring needed a brand that frames her work rather than competing with it. The answer is a strict monochrome identity anchored by a mirrored monogram.
deliverables: Logo and monogram, colour and type system, business cards, multi-page website
description: Alla Vakker has more than seven years of experience in portrait and brand photography, working with European designers, hotels and restaurants. Her work spans fashion, luxury hospitality, nightlife and fine-art nude photography, a field where a photographer’s personal brand is often the first thing a client sees.
task: Build a personal brand from scratch that feels refined and creative, slightly daring yet elegant, and credible to fashion labels and luxury hotels.
concept: The monogram joins A and V so that each letter mirrors the other, just as a photographer reflects a subject through the lens. Set in an elegant high-contrast typeface, it works both as a personal signature and as a fashion mark.
solution: The identity deliberately steps back. Black and white leave all the colour to the photographs, keeping every portfolio page and printed piece coherent however varied the images are. Personality comes through detail instead: a monogram with an idea behind it, a high-contrast typeface with a fashion sensibility, and a handwritten line that adds warmth.

gallery.title: Concept
gallery.text: The mark is a monogram built from the first letters of her first and last name. The two letters mirror each other, just as a photographer reflects the model through the lens. The logo uses an elegant, feminine typeface that reflects the brand’s values and speaks to the photographer’s audience.
